newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia sentences Yugoslav army chief to 20 years.
newsitem.headline: Croatia sentences Yugoslav army chief to 20 years.

text.p: A Croatian court sentenced the Yugoslav army chief of staff, General Momcilo Perisic, on Thursday to 20 years in prison for war crimes allegedly committed almost six years ago, Croatian radio reported.
Perisic and 18 other officers of the former Yugoslav army were tried in their absence in the county court of the coastal town of Zadar.

Perisic and four others were sentenced to 20 years in prison for their involvement in the shelling of the town and its surrounding area in September and October 1991, which resulted in the death of 34 civilians, the radio said.
The remaining 14 defendants were sentenced to terms of between 10 and 15 years. All have since left Croatia.
Perisic, the most prominent figure of the 19, was at the time the commander of the former Yugoslav army artillery school in Zadar.
He later climbed to the top position in the army of present Yugoslavia, which consists of only two of the six former republics -- Serbia and Montenegro.
The Croat-Serb 1991-95 war started when Zagreb declared independence from Serb-dominated Yugoslavia in June 1991, sparking a rebellion of its minority Serbs.
The then-powerful Yugoslav army used the rebellion as an excuse to quell the secession, moving into Croatia and shelling many of its cities, including Zadar, Dubrovnik and Vukovar.
